Evaluate Precision Against a Set of Named Tiers

Source: R/profile_eligibility.R
profile_plan_precision.Rd

Takes the raw counts from profile_audit_support and computes, for each row, how wide a confidence interval a reported proportion from that count would actually have – then marks whether that width clears each requested precision tier. Class-level rows use the Wilson score interval (single proportion); pairwise and profile rows use the conservative simultaneous Goodman interval (several proportions reported from one group at once), matching the same two interval families used in methodology/j2_support_precision/ in anumaan-analysis.

Usage

profile_plan_precision(
  support,
  tiers = c(tier1 = 5, tier2 = 7.5, tier3 = 10),
  conf_level = 0.95,
  n_categories = NULL
)

Arguments

support

One element of the list returned by profile_audit_support (i.e. $class, $pair, or $profile), or the whole list (all three are evaluated).

tiers

Named numeric vector, half-width in percentage points for each named tier, ordered from most to least demanding. Default c(tier1 = 5, tier2 = 7.5, tier3 = 10) – the same three percentage-point bars used historically for J2-L, just named plainly by rank (tier1 = narrowest interval required = hardest to clear) instead of labels like "strict"/"moderate"/"loose" that imply an interpretation this function doesn't make. Any number of tiers is fine – add a tier4, rename them, whatever a given use needs.

conf_level

Numeric. Confidence level for the interval. Default 0.95.

n_categories

Integer. Number of simultaneous categories for the Goodman interval on pair/profile rows (e.g. 4 for the RR/RS/SR/SS cells of one pair, or 2^D for a full D-class profile). Required when evaluating $pair/$profile directly; ignored for $class.

Value

The same data frame(s) as the input, with an added interval_half_width column (percentage points, at the worst-case/conservative proportion for Goodman rows) and one logical passes_<tier> column per entry in tiers (e.g. passes_tier1, passes_tier2, ...).
